result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the concept of "otherness"—the instinct to divide people into "us" and "them" based on nationality, race, religion, ideology, or any arbitrary boundary. I’d dissolve the fear and hostility that make humans see difference as a threat rather than a thread in the same fabric.

This wouldn’t erase conflict (disagreement is natural), but it would strip away the dehumanization that justifies war, oppression, and indifference. Imagine a world where no child is taught to hate before they learn to read, where resources are shared not out of charity but recognition of shared fate, where borders are porous to both people and ideas.

The ripple effects would be vast: systems built on exploitation would collapse; art, science, and culture would flourish in cross-pollination; and the energy spent on domination could redirect to healing the planet and each other.

But here’s the catch—this change wouldn’t come from magic. It would require dismantling the stories we tell ourselves about superiority, scarcity, and enemy-making. And that’s the hardest work of all.
